title: First-person: hands hold the weapon, it does not float
note: First-person: an object tagged hands exists with real geometry; a gun floating without hands is the first thing a player sees.
intent: A weapon alone in the lower right of the frame is the classic unfinished first-person view. Build a viewmodel group parented to the camera holding both the weapon and a pair of forearms and hands, with the front hand on the fore-end and the rear hand on the grip, and tag the arms group hands. Keep the viewmodel on its own near-clip range so it never intersects walls, add a small positional lag behind the camera's rotation so it feels attached to a body, and bob it with the movement speed rather than with the wall clock.

check.note: First-person: an object tagged hands (or a group holding the arms) exists with real geometry; a gun floating without hands is the first thing a player sees.

port: The mainOwner builds the viewmodel once and parents it to the active camera; the weapon facet fills it in and never adds its own camera child.
